records.category: state anti-corruption body dissolved the central bank's own governing board
records.summary: On 9 February 2020 Sudan's state anti-corruption body, the Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption and Funds Recovery Committee, dissolved the administrative board of the Central Bank of Sudan. The same decision covered the boards of 11 other banks, and the committee dismissed nine bank managers it said had ties to the former Omar al-Bashir government. The central bank's own board was the subject of the decision, not the body taking it.
records.source_title: Anti-Corruption Committee dissolves boards of Central Bank of Sudan and 11 other banks
records.quote: dissolved the administrative board of the Central Bank on Sudan (CBoS)

parties.party: Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption and Funds Recovery Committee
parties.name_as_stated: Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption, and Funds Recovery Committee

records.category: the bank's own disclosure of a staff dismissal for irregularities
records.summary: In its own Annual Report for the financial year ended 30 June 2024, the Central Bank of Samoa discloses in the Staffing section (VIII.2.1) that one of its staff was dismissed for irregularities. The Bank employed 102 staff at 30 June 2024; seven others resigned to move overseas, and one member of staff was terminated. The Bank is reporting conduct by its own employee, and it does not name the person or set out what the irregularities were.
records.source_title: Central Bank of Samoa Annual Report 2023-2024, Section VIII.2.1 Staffing
records.quote: with one (1) staff who was terminated due to staff irregularities

refused.candidate: Ali Sherif Al Emadi, convicted 2024 of bribery, abuse of position, damage to public funds and money laundering; sentenced to 20 years and fined over 61 billion riyals
refused.test_failed: Conduct in a DIFFERENT office. He held the post of Minister of Finance, and the report does not name Qatar Central Bank anywhere - not as subject, victim or party.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: A court, prosecution or official document stating that the conduct he was convicted of involved Qatar Central Bank money, or his role on the Qatar Central Bank board.

refused.candidate: Craig Orlando Walls v Bermuda Monetary Authority, Supreme Court of Bermuda 2026 No. 43, ruling of 12 June 2026 (Martin J)
refused.test_failed: The finding runs the other way. Walls, a BMA senior analyst from 2000 to 2017, was dismissed for serious misconduct after the court found he kept promoting the Bentley Friendly Society in breach of an undertaking he gave the BMA in 2014. The court struck out his claim as res judicata and an abuse of process and ordered indemnity costs against him. The ruling makes no finding of misconduct, breach or bad faith by the BMA; it only records that the BMA 'had always denied that there had been any breach of Mr Walls' rights.'
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: A Bermuda court, tribunal or Auditor General finding of improper conduct BY the Bermuda Monetary Authority or one of its officials.

refused.candidate: FICAC press release 37/2024 - Sarika Devi Raj, two counts of abuse of office
refused.test_failed: Wrong employer. She was a Finance Officer in the Accounts section of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces. The Reserve Bank of Fiji is not named.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: A FICAC release, charge sheet or Fiji High Court judgment naming a Reserve Bank of Fiji officer as the accused.

refused.candidate: FICAC press release 07/2023 - Joji Cavalevu, 12 counts falsification of documents, 12 counts obtaining financial advantage, 3 counts forgery
refused.test_failed: Wrong institution. He was the former Relationship and Sales Officer of the Fiji Development Bank, a state development bank, not the Reserve Bank of Fiji.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: The same kind of FICAC charge brought against a Reserve Bank of Fiji employee.

refused.candidate: Administrative Prosecution referral, June 2019: a treasury cashier referred to urgent trial over embezzling 3,460,000 EGP and forging the records of five branch accounts, with 13 other bank employees referred for disciplinary accountability
refused.test_failed: Wrong bank. The employer named is the Agricultural Bank of Egypt (al-Bank al-Zira'i al-Masri), a state commercial bank, not the Central Bank of Egypt.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: An Administrative Prosecution referral, indictment or court judgment that names the Central Bank of Egypt as the employer of the accused - which would also settle the 13 June 2018 bribery arrest the press only describes as 'one of the banks'.

refused.candidate: March 2022 arrests of Farah Mohamed Osman and Sahal Said Awaleh after an Auditor General / State Inspectorate-General audit found millions of dollars misappropriated
refused.test_failed: Wrong institution. Osman was deputy director of materials at the Ministry of Budget and Awaleh was director of the general treasury. Neither report names the Banque Centrale de Djibouti or any of its officials. Confirmed against a second outlet (newscentraltv.com/?p=97540), which also does not name the central bank.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: An Inspection Generale d'Etat report, Cour des Comptes report or court record naming a Banque Centrale de Djibouti official as the subject.

refused.candidate: Bahraini courts convicted the Central Bank of Iran, Future Bank and other Iranian banks of money laundering; five Future Bank officials jailed
refused.test_failed: Inversion, twice over. The Central Bank of Bahrain is the regulator that uncovered and referred the scheme - the detector, not the subject. And the central bank convicted is Iran's, so the record does not key to BHR at all.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: A Bahraini court judgment, tribunal ruling or audit finding whose subject is a Central Bank of Bahrain official or the CBB's own money. (Separately, this IS a live lead for an IRN record.)

refused.candidate: Dabanga, 29 October 2025: 'Conflicts of influence and interests confound Central Bank of Sudan' - the bank moving from supervisor to sole legal gold exporter, the dismissal of governor Burai Al-Siddiq Ali Ahmed and of deputy governor Mohamed Osman Ahmed Mohamed Khair
refused.test_failed: A characterisation, not a finding. The conflict-of-interest analysis is the opinion of an interviewed banking expert, Omar Sayed Ahmed, and the smuggling figure of 50 to 80 per cent is his estimate. The article reports no audit, inquiry or prosecution, and nobody is accused of anything. Attaching the two dismissed officials' names to it would accuse them of conduct the text does not allege.
refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: An audit, prosecution or parliamentary inquiry finding about the Central Bank of Sudan's gold-export monopoly or about either dismissed official's conduct in office.

confirmed_blank.document: Auditor-General's Office of Singapore, Annual Report FY2016/17 (ar_fy2016_17.pdf)
confirmed_blank.sections_read: Part II footnote 1 (p.24) and the list of statutory boards receiving unmodified audit opinions; Part III paragraph 5 (p.50) on the Financial Sector Development Fund
confirmed_blank.finding: The Monetary Authority of Singapore appears twice. The footnote states 'The Monetary Authority of Singapore is audited by AGO annually' and that the MAS Act provides for no other auditor, and MAS is listed among the statutory boards given an unmodified opinion. The only other appearance is the MAS Act cited as the statute governing the audit of a different entity, the Financial Sector Development Fund. No audit observation, lapse or irregularity is reported against MAS.
confirmed_blank.note: This is the second AGO year read (FY2023/24 was read in an earlier round, same result). FY2011/12 to FY2015/16, FY2017/18 to FY2022/23 and FY2024/25 remain individually unread.

needs_a_hand_check.detail: Both return HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Attention Required' interstitial, so the search form cannot be driven from here. Individual judgment pages on rms.paclii.org and pacliirms.austlii.edu.au are reachable and do surface through ordinary web search. A hand check of PacLII's own search for 'Reserve Bank of Fiji' and 'Central Bank of Samoa' as a party or as an employer is the open item.

searched_no_result.documents_read: Arabic search for Nazaha statements naming an employee of al-Bank al-Markazi al-Saudi / Mu'assasat al-Naqd as the accused
searched_no_result.finding: No statement names a Saudi Central Bank employee as an accused person. The cases returned concern a retired colonel, 120 detained government staff, a 32-person 3bn-dollar case, and a case run with the Public Investment Fund. This is consistent with the known trap: SAMA appears in Nazaha statements as a cooperating detector, not as the employer of the accused.

searched_no_result.finding: The coverage does not name the Palestine Monetary Authority anywhere, so nothing can be filed from it. The underlying report file is identified as 'annualReportAr2020' and has NOT itself been read - see leads.

searched_no_result.finding: The external audit opinion of the Controller and Chief Auditor is not inside the annual report PDF - Section IX says the audited accounts form the final section, but the document text ends before them. The separate financial-statement PDFs (see leads) carry the opinion. No emphasis-of-matter, key audit matter or fraud note was found in the report text.

searched_no_result.finding: The only CBB self-published enforcement document that surfaces is the Compliance and Enforcement Annual Report 2024, which records the CBB's actions against its licensees - the bank as detector, not subject. No CBB disclosure about its own staff discipline, conflict-of-interest declarations or procurement cancellations appears.

leads_not_opened.lead: The Palestinian Authority's Financial and Administrative Control Bureau annual reports, the Bureau's own PDFs (file name pattern 'annualReportAr2020', 2020 edition and the later years). The Bureau audits the Palestine Monetary Authority. Search the full PDF text for 'sultat al-naqd' rather than relying on press coverage, which skipped it.
leads_not_opened.why: The Bureau's report is the one document whose remit covers the PMA as an audited body, and PSE's existing record has the Ministry of Finance as subject, so a PMA-subject finding here would close it.
